flawed_step: Step 3: the claim that every 3-regular 3-connected graph can be reduced to a Hamiltonian base case by a reduction that keeps a Hamiltonian cycle when reversed. No such reduction exists, because the Petersen graph is 3-regular and 3-connected but has no Hamiltonian cycle (Steps 4–8).
counterexample: The Petersen graph. It has an outer 5-cycle u0..u4 (u_i~u_{i+1}), an inner pentagram v0..v4 (v_i~v_{i+2}) and spokes u_i v_i. It is cubic, simple, has 10 vertices and is 3-connected, but it has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary:
Proof attempt, with a verdict on every step:
1. Let G be a finite, simple, 3-regular, 3-connected graph. We want a Hamiltonian cycle. — Justified: this is just the setup.
2. Base case: K4 is 3-regular, 3-connected and Hamiltonian. — Justified.
3. Inductive step: reduce G to a smaller cubic 3-connected graph (for example by contracting a triangle or removing an edge), and lift the Hamiltonian cycle back to G. — NOT justified. Lifting a Hamiltonian cycle is not guaranteed in general. Steps 4–8 show the statement is actually false, so no such step can work.
4. Test the Petersen graph P, labelled as in the counterexample field. It is simple, has 10 vertices, and every vertex has degree 3. — Justified.
5. P is 3-connected. It is vertex-transitive and connected, and the vertex connectivity of such a graph is at least 2(d+1)/3 = 8/3. So κ ≥ 3. — Justified; this is a standard fact, and it can also be checked directly using girth 5 and diameter 2.
6. Suppose H is a Hamiltonian cycle in P. H crosses between the outer and inner vertex sets an even, nonzero number of times, so it uses 2 or 4 spokes. — Justified.
7. Case of 2 spokes. H then contains a path through all 5 outer vertices and a path through all 5 inner vertices. The outer path uses 4 edges of the outer C5, so its ends are u_i and u_{i+1}, which are adjacent. The inner path is a Hamiltonian path of the pentagram (also a C5), so its ends must be adjacent there. But v_i and v_{i+1} are not adjacent in the pentagram. Contradiction. — Justified.
8. Case of 4 spokes. Say the unused spoke is at i = 0. Then u0 uses edges u4u0 and u0u1, and v0 uses v0v2 and v0v3. Every other vertex uses its spoke plus exactly one ring edge. So u1 and u4 are already full, which forces the edge u2u3. Likewise v2 and v3 are full, which forces v1v4. Starting at u0, H then runs u0–u1–v1–v4–u4–u0. That is a closed 5-cycle, not a 10-cycle. Contradiction. — Justified.
9. So P is a 3-regular, 3-connected graph with no Hamiltonian cycle, and the statement is false. The inductive argument breaks down at Step 3. — Justified.
